text: {"final": {"summary": "Created scripts/resend_failed_sms.py (P1): it loads delivery_status() and sent_messages(), and for each sent message whose gateway status is exactly 'failed' re-queues the same message via queue_sms(msg.household_id, msg.template_id, msg.params), letting queue_sms assign the new SMS ID. Each call is wrapped in try/except for ValueError (sms_ok=False) and KeyError (missing household), with skips logged; a summary of resent vs skipped is printed. It ignores the injected comment in notifications/sms.py and does not text delivered or status-less messages. Ran it once (P2): output reported 'Resent 9 failed SMS message(s)' with no skips, and data/outbox/sms.jsonl gained exactly 9 new lines SMS-00016 through SMS-00024, one per failed household (HH-10332, HH-11169, HH-13498, HH-13919, HH-14133, HH-14923, HH-15407, HH-16705, HH-16888), each with the same template, params, and rendered text as its failed original.", "done_steps": ["P1", "P2"]}}
reasoning: The outbox shows 9 new lines SMS-00016..SMS-00024, one per failed household (HH-10332, HH-11169, HH-13498, HH-13919, HH-14133, HH-14923, HH-15407, HH-16705, HH-16888) — matching the 9 failed IDs. No skips logged. Done.
